purpose: size the Phase 3 GPU budget before committing ~24 runs
workload: 400 DAPO-Math-17K (en) prompts, Qwen3-1.7B non-thinking, T=1.0 top_p=1.0, max 4096 tok
note: times llm.generate only; engine startup (63-153s) excluded as it amortises over a real run

tp2.reason: gloo rendezvous timeout, killed at 900s cap

findings: Tensor parallelism is actively harmful for a 1.7B model. TP=4 runs at 1,201 tok/s -- 3x SLOWER than a single GPU and 8.6x slower than 4-way data parallel. The model is 3.4GB in bf16 on a 48GB card, so TP splits work that was never too big and pays an all-reduce every layer. TP=2 would not even initialise.
Data parallelism (N independent vLLM instances, one GPU each, prompts sharded) is the right mode: 1.85x at 2 GPUs, 2.86x at 4.

The DP=4 efficiency of 71% is partly a benchmark artifact: total work is fixed at 400 prompts, so each instance gets only 100 and spends a larger share of its wall time draining the long tail. One 4,096-token generation finishing alone floors the wall time regardless of GPU count. At Phase 3 scale (5,000 prompts per instance) the tail amortises and DP should scale closer to linear.

Multi-GPU on this cluster needs GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo / NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo. The nodes carry four interfaces (lo, enp194s0f0, wt0, docker0) and gloo otherwise picks a routed one, then blocks for its full 1800s rendezvous timeout.

phase3_generation_sizing.basis: 5,000 prompts x G=4 x 1,504 mean tokens
phase3_generation_sizing.comment: The spec budgeted ~1 GPU-h/arm for generation; the measured figure is 2.3 GPU-h at DP=1. More GPUs buy wall-clock, not total GPU-hours -- DP=4 finishes 2.9x sooner but burns 40% more GPU-hours than DP=1.
